value.rationale: The smallest rim length permitting any nontrivial oscillation is a natural intrinsic threshold for cyclic competition on a graph with a global hub and a local ring. Crossing it creates an explicit family of primitive periods growing exactly as 3n, while the universal fixed-point count is only 3(n+2). This is a structural finite/infinite transition and a precise unbounded period construction, not a parameter renaming, isolated tiny count or mechanical corollary of the cited lattice/tree theory.
